title: Stereoscopic visual stimuli for examining biological motion perception and unanticipated steering manoeuvres in people with Parkinson's disease
author: Foo

steps.title: Arrange laboratory equipment
steps.instruction: Place the S3D camcorder (Panasonic AG‑3DA1) on a stable tripod, set the dual front projectors (Optoma EH2060) approximately 3.20 m above the floor, and install the projection screen (2.36 m × 4.20 m). Ensure the pathway between the camcorder and screen is 1.20 m wide to limit horizontal shearing.

steps.title: Set camcorder recording parameters
steps.instruction: Configure the S3D camcorder to record in progressive mode at 30 Hz with Full HD resolution (1920 × 1080 px) from a camera height of 1.45 m. Adjust the aspect ratio to 16:9.

steps.title: Perform white‑balance and brightness matching
steps.instruction: Execute white‑balancing and brightness adjustments so that the left‑ and right‑lens images are matched before filming.

steps.title: Position calibration frame
steps.instruction: Place a surrogate calibration frame scaled to a height of 2.36 m in the centre of the pathway, ensuring it is fully within the camcorder’s field of view.

steps.title: Determine optimal filming height
steps.instruction: Systematically film test clips at camera heights ranging from 1.20 m to 1.60 m in 0.05 m increments, visually inspect each for vertical shearing and compression, and select 1.45 m as the optimal height for participants 1.50 m–1.85 m tall.

steps.title: Adjust convergence point
steps.instruction: Initially set the convergence (reference) plane to coincide with the projection screen. Then shift the calibration frame 2.00 m backward and adjust the convergence distance between 0.50 m and 2.50 m until the left and right images interlace correctly on the camcorder LCD, placing the convergence point behind the screen to compress the viewing volume.

steps.title: Provide actor cueing
steps.instruction: During filming, the investigator approaches the actor from behind the camcorder and randomly signals the actor to change direction while walking either casually or while texting, ensuring appropriate body language and facial expressions.

steps.title: Film stimulus scenes
steps.instruction: Record each scenario with the actor approaching the camcorder at a speed of 1.50 ± 0.05 m·s⁻¹. Use two timing gates to measure velocity and retain only footage that meets the speed criterion. At a predetermined moment, have the actor make an abrupt left or right change within the perturbation zone (≈5.30 m from the participant).

steps.title: Merge stereoscopic video streams
steps.instruction: Import the left‑ and right‑lens videos into Adobe After Effects CS6, combine them into a single side‑by‑side file of 3840 × 1080 px, and trim each clip to remove the actor’s gait‑initiation phase so motion starts at T1. Embed a frame of the empty background at the start and end of each trimmed clip for smooth transitions.

steps.title: Set up projection hardware
steps.instruction: Connect the Mac Pro (8 × 3.0 GHz 8‑core Intel Xeon E5, 16 GB DDR3) to the two projectors via a Matrox Dualhead2go Digital Edition multi‑display adapter and two Mini‑Cat® UH‑1BT HDMI extenders. Assign one projector to the left video stream and the other to the right stream.

steps.title: Digitally calibrate projectors
steps.instruction: Use Bourke’s PBMesh plugin with WarpPlayer to warp a mesh overlay onto the screen for each projector, aligning the images to eliminate depth‑field distortion and reduce visual fatigue.

steps.title: Configure playback software
steps.instruction: Load the custom Quartz Composer v4.0 composition (by P.D. Bourke) to control video playback, ensuring every frame (including the first) is displayed for each trial.

steps.title: Install polarizing filters
steps.instruction: Mount orthogonal linear polarizing filters (±45°) on each projector and provide participants with matching polarized glasses so that the left eye receives only the left image and the right eye only the right image.

steps.title: Synchronize video with participant position
steps.instruction: Place customized timing gates and connect them to the interface unit to trigger video playback when a participant reaches the perturbation zone, adjusting gate positions as needed to accommodate each participant’s self‑selected walking velocity.
